candidates.name: Cancer (General)
candidates.rationale: 1 user selected Cancer (General) and free-text terms 'cancer' and 'lungs' appear, indicating a gap not covered by the current list.

supplements.name: Vitamin D
supplements.reason: May support immune function and has been studied in cancer prevention.
supplements.evidence: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements (2023). Vitamin D Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminD-HealthProfessional/

supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids
supplements.reason: May reduce inflammation and has been associated with lower cancer risk in some studies.
supplements.interactions: May increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants
supplements.evidence: Manson JE, et al. (2019). Marine n-3 Fatty Acids and Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer. N Engl J Med. PMID: 30415628

warnings: Do not use as a substitute for cancer screening or treatment
Consult oncologist before starting any supplement
avoid: High-dose antioxidants during chemotherapy without medical advice

lifestyle.advice: Emphasize a plant-based diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
Engage in at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity per week.

candidates.name: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)
candidates.rationale: Symptoms 'Low Energy' and 'Muscle Weakness' were reported by users with no condition, suggesting a gap for chronic fatigue conditions.

supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10
supplements.reason: May improve energy production in mitochondria and reduce fatigue.
supplements.interactions: May interact with blood pressure medications
supplements.evidence: Castro-Marrero J, et al. (2016). Effect of Coenzyme Q10 Plus Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide on Mitochondrial Function and Fatigue in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. J Clin Med. PMID: 27164194

supplements.name: Magnesium
supplements.reason: May help with muscle weakness and energy metabolism.
supplements.timing: With food to reduce GI upset
supplements.interactions: May interact with some antibiotics and diuretics
supplements.evidence: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements (2022). Magnesium Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Not a substitute for medical diagnosis
May require gradual dosing to avoid GI side effects

lifestyle.advice: Pacing and graded exercise therapy under professional guidance.
Maintain a consistent sleep schedule and practice sleep hygiene.

candidates.name: Lung Disease (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)
candidates.rationale: Free-text term 'lungs' appears, and no respiratory condition beyond Asthma is on the list; COPD is common in the Philippines due to smoking and biomass exposure.

supplements.name: Vitamin D
supplements.reason: May reduce exacerbations in COPD patients with deficiency.
supplements.evidence: Jolliffe DA, et al. (2019). Vitamin D to prevent exacerbations of COPD: systematic review and meta-analysis. Thorax. PMID: 31203270

supplements.name: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC)
supplements.reason: May reduce mucus viscosity and oxidative stress in COPD.
supplements.interactions: May interact with nitroglycerin and some antibiotics
supplements.evidence: Decramer M, et al. (2005). Effects of N-acetylcysteine on outcomes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Lancet. PMID: 15950031

warnings: Not a replacement for bronchodilators or inhaled corticosteroids
avoid: High-dose NAC in patients with peptic ulcer disease

lifestyle.advice: Maintain a healthy weight and avoid high-sodium foods.

candidates.name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
candidates.rationale: PCOS is common in the Philippines and often undiagnosed; it is not on the current list but is a frequent comorbidity with conditions like Diabetes and Obesity.

supplements.name: Inositol (myo-inositol)
supplements.reason: Improves insulin sensitivity and ovarian function in PCOS.
supplements.evidence: Unfer V, et al. (2017). Myo-inositol effects in women with PCOS: a meta-analysis. Gynecol Endocrinol. PMID: 27898267

supplements.name: Vitamin D
supplements.reason: Deficiency is common in PCOS and may worsen metabolic parameters.
supplements.evidence: Endocrine Society (2020). Vitamin D and PCOS. https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/pcos-and-vitamin-d

warnings: Not a substitute for hormonal therapy or fertility treatment
Monitor blood glucose if using inositol with diabetes medications

lifestyle.advice: Low glycemic index diet to manage insulin resistance.
At least 30 minutes of moderate exercise most days.

candidates.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
candidates.rationale: IBS is already on the list, but the free-text narrative includes 'looks' which may relate to stool appearance; however, to avoid duplication, this candidate is replaced with another condition. Instead, I propose 'Chronic Constipation' as a distinct condition not covered.

supplements.name: Psyllium Husk
supplements.reason: Increases stool bulk and promotes regularity.
supplements.interactions: May reduce absorption of some medications; take 2 hours apart
supplements.evidence: American College of Gastroenterology (2021). Clinical Guideline: Management of Chronic Constipation. Am J Gastroenterol. PMID: 33929376

supplements.name: Magnesium Citrate
supplements.reason: Osmotic laxative effect to relieve constipation.
supplements.interactions: May interact with some antibiotics and diuretics
supplements.evidence: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements (2022). Magnesium Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not use if experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting
avoid: Long-term use of stimulant laxatives without medical advice

lifestyle.advice: Increase fiber intake gradually and drink plenty of water.
Regular physical activity to stimulate bowel movements.

candidates.name: Sleep Apnea (Snoring / Paused Breathing)
candidates.rationale: Sleep Apnea is already on the list, but the statistics show no direct count; however, it is a common comorbidity with Obesity and Hypertension. To avoid duplication, I propose 'Restless Legs Syndrome' as a distinct sleep-related condition not covered.
symptomPool: urge to move legs at night

supplements.name: Iron (Ferrous Sulfate)
supplements.reason: Iron deficiency is a common cause of RLS; supplementation may reduce symptoms.
supplements.timing: On an empty stomach with vitamin C for absorption
supplements.interactions: May interact with antacids and some antibiotics
supplements.evidence: Allen RP, et al. (2014). Restless legs syndrome: diagnostic criteria, special considerations, and treatment. Sleep Med. PMID: 24680205

supplements.name: Magnesium
supplements.reason: May help relax muscles and improve sleep quality.
supplements.interactions: May interact with some antibiotics and diuretics
supplements.evidence: National Institutes of Health Office of Dietary Supplements (2022). Magnesium Fact Sheet for Health Professionals. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Magnesium-HealthProfessional/

warnings: Do not use iron if ferritin levels are normal or high
avoid: Caffeine and alcohol in the evening

lifestyle.advice: Establish a regular sleep schedule and avoid stimulating activities before bed.
Moderate exercise during the day may reduce symptoms.

summary: The biggest gaps are the absence of Cancer (General) and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, which are directly hinted by user-reported conditions and symptoms. Additionally, common Philippine conditions like PCOS and chronic constipation are missing, and Restless Legs Syndrome addresses a sleep-related gap not covered by existing options.
